paper_title: A Bookworm Climbs up the Polynomial Hierarchy: Meta-Restoration Complexity in Arithmetic Puzzles
classifications: Theory of computation → Problems, reductions and completeness
statement: We conclude with some open questions. 1. In this paper we explored the complexity of formulae involving nested ∃!x quantifiers. What can be said about other similar types of quantifiers? For instance, we could consider quantifiers such as “there exist exactly two x satisfying P (x)” and “exactly half of all x satisfy P (x)”. 2. Are there natural examples of parsimonious reductions that are not locally parsimonious? 3. Regarding the hardness of meta-level additive restorations: While we have shown that level-2 additive restorations admit a polynomial-time algorithm, the computational complexity of level-k additive or subtractive restorations for k > 2 remains open. Do such problems climb higher in the polynomial hierarchy, or can they still be solved efficiently?
